subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To draw a blank

options.text: To be unsuccessful at eliciting a response

solution:
The correct answer is '**To be unsuccessful at eliciting a response**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate** meaning of the given idiom ' **To draw a blank**' is '**To be unsuccessful at eliciting a response**'.
 
• **To draw a blank**: *to get no result or response*.__
 __
 
• **E.g.** *Detectives investigating the case have drawn a blank so far__.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the **correct answer** is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Let's look at some similar idioms.
 
 
• **Fight a losing battle**- *to try hard to do something when there is no chance that you will succeed*

 
 
• *The police are fighting a losing battle against a rising tide of crime*__.
 
 
 
• **Flog a dead horse**- *waste energy on a lost cause or a situation that cannot be changed*. 
 __
 
• *He keeps trying to get it published but I think he's flogging a dead horse*__.
 
 
 
• **Running on empty**- *have exhausted all of one's resources*.
 __
 
• He was running on empty and even the alcohol had worn off__.
